title: Lanelet Prioritizer — personal prod/experiment scratchpad
content:
Quick context / one-liner:

Lanelet = a tiny, per-session/per-user routing + fidelity policy that decides which response lane to use for each request (cheap, medium, premium).
Goal: let product teams get deterministic cost savings while preserving critical quality for a subset of queries. Think: micro-QoS with cheap fallbacks and graceful fidelity escalation.

Why I'm sketching this here (notes to self):
- Hosted API teams need predictable unit economics without forcing users to completely re-architect prompts.
- We have batching/caching/quantization levers but lack a small, user-facing primitive to express per-request fidelity intent.
- Should be lightweight enough to expose in SDK + Console as presets.

Problem framing:
- Many apps have a small % of queries that require high fidelity (legal advice, code gen) and a large tail that is fine with cheaper outputs (search summarization, short replies).
- Currently teams either use global model weights or write complex prompt logic. No built-in lane that automatically applies cheaper model/config for safe queries.

Principles / constraints:
- Non-breaking: default behavior stays same for existing customers.
- Transparent: teams must be able to see cost and accuracy tradeoffs per lane in Console.
- Fast path: SDK-level flag plus server-side inference routing with autoscaling respected.
- Conservative fallback: if cheap lane looks uncertain, escalate to medium/premium rather than returning low-quality result silently.

Rough feature surface (ideas):
- Lane presets: cheap | balanced | premium (names TBD).
- Lane condition: static (user-provided tag) or dynamic (confidence classifier + policy).
- Confidence signal: small verifier model runs cheaply on prefix to predict quality risk.
- Escalation policy: instant re-run on premium if confidence low, with rate-limited budget.
- Billing: token-level attribution by lane + re-run cost attribution.
- Console views: lane-level traffic split, cost delta, quality regressions (linked to eval sets).

Mini PRD outline (very rough):
- Problem: expensive one-size-fits-all inference for varied query criticality.
- Solution: introduce per-request "lanelet" attribute that routes to pre-configured model/runtime configs with optional dynamic checks.
- Success metrics: 15-30% unit cost reduction for early adopters; <2% uplift in perceived error for cheap lane across monitored evals.
- Non-goals: not replacing full canary/rollout infra or tuned prompt engineering.

User stories (raw):
- As an engineer, I want to mark a request as "cheap-cue" so it uses lower-cost model and returns faster for non-critical tasks.
- As a product manager, I want to see lane-level cost and outcome metrics so I can tune traffic allocation.
- As an ops engineer, I want automatic escalation when cheap lane fails a confidence check so users don't get garbage silently.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- API supports lanelet param (string) and accepts predefined lane names.
- Router can map lane to model variant + runtime config.
- Console shows per-lane token counts and estimated cost delta.
- Escalation path triggers at least 90% of detected low-confidence cheap responses to premium re-run in experiment.

Metrics to track (for pilot):
- tokens_per_request_by_lane (median + p95)
- latency_by_lane (p50/p95)
- cost_per_1000_requests_by_lane
- escalation_rate (percent of cheap responses re-run)
- quality_delta_by_lane (via small eval prompt-set; automated A/B)

Experiments to run (sequence):
1) Internal traffic-only pilot: route 10% of internal app traffic to lanelets with static tags to validate cost math.
2) Confidence classifier A/B: run classifier on cheap lane in shadow mode for 2 weeks, measure false negatives.
3) Auto-escalation opt-in: enable re-runs for 5% of cheap traffic, measure user-visible regressions and cost.

Rough rollout plan:
- Phase 0: SDK + API param + Console read-only metrics (2 sprints).
- Phase 1: Manual lane presets + routing + billing attribution (2 sprints).
- Phase 2: Confidence verifier + automated escalation + eval hooks (3 sprints).
- Phase 3: Productize presets in Console with 1-click enable + docs + sample prompts (2 sprints).

API sketch (very rough):
// request body
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "lanelet": "cheap",          // one of: cheap|balanced|premium or custom
  "lane_metadata": {"caller_intent":"search-summary"},
  "escalation_budget": 1        // how many re-runs allowed per 100 reqs
}

Server-side behavior (notes):
- If lanelet == cheap: route to quantized model variant, lower beam/temperature, enable prefix caching aggressively.
- Run quick verifier (tiny model) in parallel (shadow) — if below confidence threshold, trigger escalation.
- Billing: charge for initial run + any escalation runs. Attribute accordingly in usage logs.

Console UX notes (sketch):
- Lanelet config page: name, model variant, verifier threshold, escalation budget, expected cost savings estimate.
- Live view: traffic %, cost delta, escalation events, linked eval failures.
- Simple presets: "Economy", "Balanced", "Accuracy-First" with expected cost delta and description.

Risks & open questions (brain dump):
- Verifier cost: running another model even cheap adds overhead — need to make verifier <3ms ideally or run as cheap classifier.
- Billing clarity: users will be upset if hidden re-run costs appear; must make billing transparent and opt-in.
- Migration: how to make sure existing customers don't get surprise behavior when SDK adds lane param. Default must be null/no-change.
- Fairness/regulatory: cheaper models might regress for specific demographics or edge cases — need evals per segment.
- Multi-tenant capacity: cheap lane could saturate certain pools; need routing quotas.

Open design decisions to resolve quickly:
- Should verifier run for every cheap request or sample? (tradeoff: cost vs safety)
- Should escalation be immediate re-run or async with fast fallback + later re-eval (UX tradeoffs)?
- How to let customers opt-in to free re-runs vs charge escalations? free for first N per month?

Immediate TODOs (me-focused):
- Draft a one-pager for the product weekly (due next Tues) — include sample metric graphs. (JIRA LANE-72)
- Prototype a tiny verifier in python using distilled bert -> measure latency on cpu. (GH: prior/proto/exp47)
- Slack thread: start #lanelets-discuss and seed with this doc and cost calc (done as link).

Notes to self / stream of consciousness: 
- Could combine lanelets with session-presets: session-level default lane + per-request override.
- Maybe a "lanelet hint" in response meta that indicates confidence score so downstream apps can decide to surface "may be low confidence" to users.
- Think about ML ops: need per-lane eval suites to detect quality regressions after model updates. Hook into Optimize alerts.


End of draft. Will iterate after I build the small verifier POC and get initial telemetry.
